origin.description: Replace each brace with the value of the expression inside it.
origin.usage: glue(..., .sep = "", .envir = parent.frame(), .open = "{", .close = "}", .na = "NA", .null = character(), .comment = "#", .literal = FALSE, .transformer = identity_transformer, .trim = TRUE)

arguments.name: parts
arguments.text: Unnamed strings are the template. Named arguments are values the braces can see.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Text placed between the template strings before interpolation.

arguments.name: envir
arguments.text: Extra names. When omitted, the caller's names are visible.

arguments.name: open
arguments.text: Opening delimiter. Doubling it inserts one copy.

arguments.name: close
arguments.text: Closing delimiter. Doubling it inserts one copy.

arguments.name: na
arguments.text: Replacement for a missing piece. None keeps the whole row missing.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Remove the common indent with trim before scanning.

origin.details: Several template strings are joined first. The result is a character vector long enough for the longest brace.
origin.value: A character vector of class glue.
origin.example:
name <- "Fred"
age <- 50
cat(as.character(glue("My name is {name}, my age next year is {age + 1}.")), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Replace each brace with a Python expression evaluated against the names in scope.
translation.usage: glue(*parts, sep="", envir=None, open="{", close="}", na="NA", null=<empty>, comment="#", literal=False, transformer=None, trim=True, **names)

arguments.name: parts
arguments.text: Unnamed strings are the template. Named arguments are values the braces can see.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Text placed between the template strings before interpolation.

arguments.name: envir
arguments.text: Extra names. When omitted, the caller's names are visible.

arguments.name: open
arguments.text: Opening delimiter. Doubling it inserts one copy.

arguments.name: close
arguments.text: Closing delimiter. Doubling it inserts one copy.

arguments.name: na
arguments.text: Replacement for a missing piece. None keeps the whole row missing.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Remove the common indent with trim before scanning.

translation.details: Braces run as Python. {age + 1} is computed. A name such as Petal.Length is looked up whole, so the dot is not an attribute. An f-string is not a substitute: it does not double a brace, trim, or recycle pieces.
translation.value: A Glue vector. One element compares equal to that string.
translation.example:
from glue import glue
name = "Fred"
age = 50
print(glue("My name is {name}, my age next year is {age + 1}."))
